result.note: Tests the US trade-law tools named in the story (IEEPA, Sections 122 and 301), the target of the March 2026 investigation, and the 18% baseline in the India–US interim framework.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about US trade measures affecting India in early 2026:
items: The White House used Section 122 of the Trade Act to impose a temporary 15% global tariff that expires in late July 2026.
Tariffs under Section 301 rest on presidential discretion rather than on formal investigations.
The India–US framework for an interim trade deal, reached in February 2026, set an 18% baseline tariff on Indian goods.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Section 301 builds on formal investigations and findings of unfair trade practices, not presidential discretion, which gives its levies a stronger legal footing. Section 301 could override the 18% baseline with higher, sector-specific duties.
questions.source: It builds on formal investigations and findings of unfair trade practices rather than presidential discretion, giving any resulting levies a stronger legal foundation.

questions.prompt: In early 2026, the US Supreme Court struck down tariffs imposed by President Trump under which law?
options: Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act
questions.explain: The Court struck down Trump's emergency tariffs under IEEPA, after which the White House pivoted to Section 122 for a temporary 15% global tariff. Section 301 is the replacement strategy for when that expires.
questions.source: This new development comes weeks after the Supreme Court struck down Trump’s emergency tariffs under IEEPA, which we covered here.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, the US launched a Section 301 investigation into trading partners including India, the EU and China. What did the investigation target?
options: Digital services taxes on US firms
questions.explain: Washington framed the probe around what it calls structural excess capacity in manufacturing. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer hoped to conclude it before the temporary tariffs expire in July.
questions.source: targeting what Washington calls structural excess capacity in manufacturing
